hero.title: Give AI-built applications a governed home.
hero.description: Across large enterprises, thousands of employees now build working applications with AI coding tools — most of them outside engineering. Creation has scaled; the operating model has not. This site sets out the case for a governed platform underneath that activity: what breaks today, how the alternatives compare across the six lifecycle stages, and how to build the business case for your own organisation.

whys.title: Creation has scaled. The operating model has not.
whys.body: Employees turn ideas into working apps with AI coding tools faster than any review process was designed for — and most of them sit outside engineering. Those apps still need identity, bounded data access, audit trails and cost attribution that an existing Kubernetes path was never meant to provide at this volume.

whys.title: Every ungoverned week makes the standard harder.
whys.body: Apps that ship without a governed path accumulate shared credentials, unknown data access and unowned operations. The longer the sprawl runs, the more expensive the eventual standard becomes — you end up migrating a live estate instead of setting a default.

whys.title: Buy the governed layer, not another integration project.
whys.body: Assessed hands-on across all six lifecycle stages, Vercel is the only end-to-end fit. The alternatives cover parts of the lifecycle and leave you to assemble, govern and operate the rest yourself.

sections.title: Four ways into the same argument
sections.description: Start wherever the conversation is. Each section stands on its own and links back into the others.

items.title: Capabilities
items.description: The target operating model stage by stage — what a governed path actually has to do, from first prompt to long-term maintenance.

items.title: Competitor analysis

items.title: Business case
items.description: The argument for giving citizen-built software a governed home. Every lifecycle stage makes two claims — one about the value created, one about the risk removed — each backed by evidence rather than asserted numbers.

items.title: Running a POC
items.description: Who to involve and what to prove. The roles that need to be in the room for an evaluation to produce a decision rather than a demo.

comparison.title: Vercel against the alternatives, across the lifecycle
comparison.description: A roll-up of the full capability matrix across the six lifecycle stages. Best point solution shows the strongest single vendor per stage; open any row for the per-capability verdicts, rationale and sources.
comparison.footnote: Verdicts roll up the per-capability Yes / Partial / No assessments from the current research export. Covered ≥ 85% · Partial ≥ 50% · Gap below.

closing.title: This play was proven on a real deployment.
closing.body: The capability assessments and the arguments in the business case come out of a full enterprise evaluation with a global business running AI-assisted app development at scale. The specifics of that deal are not reproduced here — what carries over is the structure, the evidence and the questions worth asking.
